title: Probe first, then fine-tune, actually trained: one extra opening epoch trains only the head on the FROZEN ImageNet trunk before the usual fine-tune (LP-FT; re-run of experiment 21, which never reached a GPU)
hypothesis: Experiment 21's hypothesis was never tested. Its run died before training on an infrastructure error: train_berlin.log ends in botocore EndpointConnectionError ('Could not connect to the endpoint URL: https://ec2.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/'), so the scorer recorded 1e9 and the harness marked it REVERTED. That verdict says nothing about LP-FT, exactly as experiment 17's crash said nothing about ring pooling (re-run as 18) and experiment 24's said nothing about Noisy Student weights (re-run as 25); issue #13 has since stopped cloud failures passing as refuted ideas. The champion is still experiment 20 (0.0777: truedop_2024 usable 93.0%, false 0.75% = 3 frames, abstain 6.25% = 25 frames; the three training photographs 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints), and model/ is identical to the code experiment 21 branched from, so its reasoning stands unchanged. The reasoning: every large step on the never-seen photograph this era came from what the pretrained trunk brought with it (exp 12 MobileNetV3-Small 10.75% -> 49.5% usable; exp 16 MobileNetV2 86.75%; exp 19 EfficientNet-B0 92.5%), and exp 20 showed that HOW the trunk is trained still moves the held-out number (a better point on the same trajectory: +0.5 usable, false 1.0% -> 0.75%). Today the trunk is fine-tuned from step 1 jointly with a randomly initialised head (prototypes std 0.01 over 2,970 tiles, random lifts, random embed BatchNorm), so the earliest, largest gradients into the pretrained blocks come from a head that knows no tile yet, and the trunk BatchNorm statistics start drifting at the same moment. Kumar et al. (ICLR 2022, 'Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution') show that full fine-tuning from a random head distorts pretrained features along in-domain directions and costs out-of-distribution accuracy while in-domain accuracy is unchanged; training the head on the frozen trunk first (LP-FT) removes most of that loss. That is our split precisely: in-domain saturated at 100%, held-out survey at 93%. It also answers the plateau the right way: the last three trained experiments (22 continuous vantages, 23 cross-survey consistency loss, 25 Noisy Student init) changed sampling, loss and init and none moved the held-out number beyond noise; the one stage never questioned since exp 12 is the trunk's fine-tuning procedure ('0.1x LR from step 1'). Exp 25 is mild evidence against a pure 'better init' story, which makes the complementary question - does the fine-tune PRESERVE whatever the init brings - the informative next test. Builds on experiment 20 (champion) and lifts experiment 21's never-run implementation verbatim.
method: model/train.py only: prepend HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS = 1 extra epoch before the existing fine-tuning run. During it every member's pretrained trunk (m.trunk: EfficientNet-B0 features[0..7]) is frozen - requires_grad False on all trunk parameters and m.trunk kept in eval mode, so its BatchNorm running stats stay at their ImageNet values and stochastic depth is off - and only the head parameters (both 1x1 lifts, embed BatchNorm1d, prototypes, offset head) train, at the head LR 1e-3, with the same losses, augmentation, MixStyle and paired-survey batches as today. After that epoch the trunk is unfrozen and the existing EPOCHS-epoch run follows exactly as now (trunk at 0.1x, cosine LR multiplier 1.0 -> 0.1 over those EPOCHS epochs, weight averaging from fine-tune epoch EPOCHS//2+1, BN recalibration, export). Total epochs = EPOCHS + 1; the warm-up epoch is cheaper than a normal one (no trunk backward). The implementation is lifted verbatim from experiment 21's never-executed model_src/train.py.
expected_outcome: On truedop_2024, 400 frames (one frame = 0.25 points): mission 0.078 -> ~0.055-0.070; usable_fix_rate 93.0% -> ~94-95% (abstentions converting to usable fixes as each member's tile belief on the foreign photograph rides less-distorted ImageNet features and the two members agree more often); false_fix_rate at or below 0.75%; abstain 6.25% -> ~4.5-5.5%. train_capture_diagnostics stay ~100% usable / 0% false; median error ~36 m unchanged; model size (31.7 MB) and host latency (~49 ms) identical - same graph. Signals to read in train_berlin.log: after the warm-up epoch, top1 on training views should already be substantial (near zero would mean the probe was too short and the experiment tests less than intended); end-of-run xs_cos_same / xsurvey_agree at or above experiment 20's. Refutation: usable flat or down (within +-2 frames counts as flat) with training diagnostics unchanged says feature distortion by the random head is not what limits the survey gap here (plausibly the 0.1x trunk LR and weight averaging already protect the features), and that the remaining ~7% need new information - a different view of the frame, or more photographs - rather than a gentler fine-tune.
init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for 1 epoch, then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
eli5: The model's 'eyes' were borrowed from a network that had already looked at a million everyday photos, and that borrowed vision is what lets it recognise Berlin in a photograph it has never seen. Until now we started teaching the eyes and the brand-new 'map-reading' part at the same moment - so in the first hours the confused new part was yanking the borrowed eyes around. Now the map-reading part first practises for one round with the eyes held still, and only then are both tuned together, so the eyes keep more of what made them useful. (This idea was planned once before, but the rented computer could not be reached, so it was never actually tried.)

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description; the weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours - both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: probe first, then fine-tune. One extra opening epoch trains only the map-reading parts (lifts, tile directions, offset head) while the borrowed ImageNet eyes are held completely still (weights and normalisation statistics frozen). Then the usual 8 epochs follow unchanged: cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, and the average of the second half's weights is what flies

implementation_brief:
FASTEST CORRECT PATH: this is a re-run of experiment 21, whose implementation was written against EXACTLY the current code and never executed because AWS was unreachable. model/model.py today is identical to runs/20261102_030305_experiment21/model_src/model.py, and model/train.py differs from runs/20261102_030305_experiment21/model_src/train.py only by the LP-FT change (verified at design time with diff). So: (1) diff the two train.py files and confirm the difference is only the items in the spec below; (2) copy runs/20261102_030305_experiment21/model_src/train.py over model/train.py; leave model/model.py untouched; (3) rename the docstring paragraph heading 'HEAD WARM-UP (experiment 21, LP-FT)' to 'HEAD WARM-UP (experiment 26, LP-FT; designed as experiment 21, which never reached a GPU)'; (4) smoke-check: the module imports, and if practical a run_epoch(..., max_chunks=1, freeze_trunk=True) step leaves every trunk parameter numerically unchanged with .grad None and the trunk BN running stats unchanged, while head parameters do change.

SPEC (what that file implements; also what to write from scratch if the copy is unusable for any reason). Edit model/train.py ONLY; model/model.py untouched (graph, parameter count, ONNX export identical to experiment 20).

1. Module constant next to AVG_EVERY: `HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS = 1  # extra opening epoch(s): head trains on the FROZEN pretrained trunk (LP-FT)`.

2. run_epoch(): add keyword argument `freeze_trunk: bool = False`. Right after its existing `model.train()` call, if freeze_trunk: for each member `m.trunk.eval()` (BN running stats frozen at ImageNet values, stochastic depth off). MixStyle is a separate module on the Member (not inside m.trunk), so it stays in train mode and keeps mixing - intended. In train_area, set `p.requires_grad_(False)` on every trunk parameter before the warm-up epoch(s) and `requires_grad_(True)` after. Do not otherwise change run_epoch's loss, targets, augmentation, statistics or bf16-autocast logic; anything iterating over grads must tolerate None. survey_diag() and recalibrate_bn() call model.train()/model.eval() themselves and are unaffected; the next run_epoch with freeze_trunk False puts the trunk back in train mode.

3. train_area(): build the optimiser and LambdaLR exactly as now (trunk group at 1e-3*TRUNK_LR_MULT, head at 1e-3; multiplier 0.1 + 0.9*0.5*(1+cos(pi*e/epochs)), epochs = CLI value). Before the existing `for epoch in range(epochs)` loop, a warm-up loop `for w in range(HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS)` that: runs run_epoch(..., averager=None, freeze_trunk=True), does NOT call sched.step() (head at constant 1e-3; the fine-tune schedule starts fresh at multiplier 1.0 afterwards), runs survey_diag, and prints a log line like the per-epoch line prefixed `[area] warmup (frozen trunk) {w+1}/{HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS}` with loss, top1, mean_max_softmax, top1_by_capture, member_top1, agree_rate and the survey_diag fields. Then unfreeze and run the existing fine-tune loop COMPLETELY unchanged: same epochs count, same sched.step() per epoch, same averaging start avg_start = epochs // 2 (0-based within the fine-tune loop), same BN recalibration and export. Do NOT rebuild the optimiser: the head's Adam state carries over; the trunk's starts fresh at unfreeze.

4. Returned metrics dict: keep every existing key; "epochs" stays the CLI fine-tune value; add "head_warmup_epochs", "total_epochs" (epochs + HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS), "warmup_top1", "warmup_member_top1", "warmup_agree_rate", "warmup_clean_top1". "init" becomes "pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS epoch(s), then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR"; append ", head-only warm-up epoch on the frozen trunk before fine-tuning (LP-FT)" to "capture_sampling"; n_train_crops / distinct_vantages_seen count the warm-up epoch too ((epochs + HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS) * len(crops) * n_caps).

5. A 'HEAD WARM-UP' paragraph in the train.py module docstring describing the above, in the style of the existing per-experiment paragraphs.

CONTRACTS TO PRESERVE (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged - `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket K] [--seed S]`, writing <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx; the ONNX contract in model/model.py's docstring - input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1]; export via model.model.export_onnx unchanged; exported fp32 ONNX <= 32 MiB (today 31.7 MB, unchanged since the graph is unchanged) and host latency <= 250 ms. Training reads only buckets(meta, "train") via the existing load_scene() - nothing under model/ may open the truedop_2024 eval capture in any form. Keep all per-view work on the device and add no .item()/.cpu() host syncs inside the step loop. Keep weight averaging, BN recalibration, MixStyle, committee, augmentation, margin loss and the bf16-autocast-on-CUDA path exactly as they are.
